newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syrian programmes to save water, environment.
newsitem.headline: Syrian programmes to save water, environment.

text.p: Syria has started implementing programmes to save water resources, eliminate pollution caused by industrial and electricity projects and to preserve some kinds of agricultural products, a U.N. official said on Wednesday.
The United Nation Development Programme (UNDP) officer in Syria said the U.N is helping Syria carry out some five programmes which are expected to be completed in five years or less.
Abdullah Al-Dardari told Reuters that Syria was included in a programme covering Arab countries to the east of the Mediterranean to preserve agricultural products, especially wheat.
The total cost of this programme is $9 million and for this the U.N. provides technical equipment and training for experts, he said.
Syria, which has produced over 4.2 million tonnes of wheat in 1996, started exporting its hard durum wheat in 1994 after achieving self sufficiency.

Dardari said the second programme, which costs $4.1 million, aimes at minimising pollution caused by the electricity generation station in Banyas, around 300 km (200 miles) from Damascus on the Syrian coast.
He said this programme will provide a new maintainance system and help cut down the use of fuel in the station.
Syria has suggested three other programmes to control environmental pollution and preserve water resources, he added.
The first programme will cost $4 million and aims at controlling pollution in the city of Aleppo, some 400 km (250 miles) north of Damascus.
The second, costing $1 million, is to help make the best use of the waters of the drainage station which will produce 500,000 cubic meters per day
The third is to rehabilitate the ancient water network in old Damascus, which is 3000 years old. The cost is $500,000.
